subject: Albert Einstein
overview: Albert Einstein changed how physicists understood **space, time and light**. Born in Germany, he worked out special relativity while employed at a Swiss patent office, published his new equations for gravity while working in Berlin, and later settled in Princeton, New Jersey.

key_moments.title: Special relativity from Bern
key_moments.text: While working at the patent office, Einstein published a paper on **special relativity** in which light travels at a fixed speed in empty space. In a separate paper he treated light as packets of energy to explain how it can knock electrons out of a material. It was his work on this effect that the **1921 Nobel Prize** citation singled out.

key_moments.title: An eclipse tests general relativity
key_moments.text: Einstein’s **new theory of gravity** predicted that the Sun would bend the light from distant stars. During the eclipse, astronomers could photograph stars near the darkened Sun and see whether their apparent positions shifted. Two sets of measurements agreed with his prediction, and news of the result made him internationally famous.

key_moments.title: Exile in Princeton
key_moments.text: Einstein had accepted a post at the **Institute for Advanced Study** the year before, intending to divide his time between Princeton and Berlin. After the Nazis took power, he gave up his German citizenship in March. He arrived in the United States in October and made Princeton his home.

key_moments.title: A warning for Roosevelt
key_moments.text: Einstein signed a letter warning **Franklin D. Roosevelt** that Germany might develop an atomic bomb. It urged the administration to move quickly on nuclear research. The letter was dated in August. The economist **Alexander Sachs** met with Roosevelt in October to discuss it.

deep_facts.text: A refrigerator can run on heat. Einstein and **Leó Szilárd** devised a cooling system that used a source such as a gas flame to drive the process. A U.S. patent granted in 1930 for one of their designs named them as inventors, though their refrigerators never reached customers.
In **1946**, Einstein accepted an honorary doctorate at **Lincoln University** in Pennsylvania, a university founded to educate Black students. He gave a lecture during the visit.

After **Chaim Weizmann** died in 1952, Einstein was offered the presidency of Israel. He turned it down. He also wrote separately to **Azriel Carlebach**, the newspaper editor who had publicly backed the idea.

connections.name: General relativity
connections.connection: Einstein published the equations for his theory of gravity in 1915 and set out the theory in a longer exposition the following year.

connections.name: Max Planck
connections.connection: Planck and Walther Nernst persuaded Einstein to move from Zurich to Berlin.

connections.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
connections.connection: Roosevelt wrote back to Einstein in 1939 to say he had set up a committee to study uranium.

connections.name: Leó Szilárd
connections.connection: Szilárd helped prepare the 1939 warning that Einstein signed for President Roosevelt.

connections.name: Bertrand Russell
connections.connection: Russell asked Einstein to sign a statement warning about nuclear war and presented it in London in 1955.

connections.name: Marie Curie
connections.connection: Einstein wrote to Curie in 1911 to offer support while she was under attack in the French press.
